obtained.how: the author's M.Sc. thesis, open download from Dalhousie University's institutional repository (Scholaris); chapter 3 (Milipsigate Lake chain pickerel and smallmouth bass) read in full, chapter 2 (Atlantic whitefish) skimmed for relevance

bibliography.note: Ava J.A. Sergio, M.Sc. thesis, Dalhousie University, Halifax, submitted March 2026; chapter 3 runs pp. 28–56 (PDF pp. 40–68). A thesis chapter, not peer-reviewed

claims.claim: Milipsigate Lake, Nova Scotia: 336 ha, 17 m deep
claims.quote: maximum depth of 17 m at peak water levels in spring and fall
claims.conditions: 335.8 ha, island-studded (both values from Ginn et al. 2008); oligotrophic, little vegetation, rocky shallows and silt at depth; the thesis says deeper layers stratify and go anoxic in summer (p. 52); 2018 water-column means 2.6 °C in Dec–Feb and 18 °C in Jun–Aug
claims.note: a cooler, deeper, stratifying lake than Hot Brook

claims.claim: half of all depth-tag detections of tagged adult chain pickerel fell between 0.76 and 1.82 m
claims.quote: 50% of detections occurred between 0.76 to 1.82 m depth
claims.conditions: adult pickerel tagged with pressure-sensing acoustic tags (V9TP), caught by angling Sept 1–Oct 19 2018, tracked to July 2019; of 18 tagged, 3 were never detected, 1 died and 6 left the array within two weeks, leaving 3,584 filtered positions; maxima > 10 m in October, November and July
claims.note: few fish behind it: the rewrite could say 'the 8 pickerel tracked beyond two weeks'

claims.source_value: the abstract and discussion say pickerel depth use 'did not change significantly over time', but the results report a significant month effect for pickerel (F = 249.66, p < 0.001; bass F = 1420) and model-predicted depths of 0–2.5 m from October to April deepening to ~8 m in August
claims.quote: Predicted depths then decreased from 2.5 m in April to ~ 8 m in August
claims.conditions: GAM D1 with a cyclic month smooth by species, bathymetry, position and fish length; 'decreased' here means deeper
claims.note: the thesis contradicts itself; safer: 'pickerel stayed shallow year-round, with a smaller seasonal change in depth than the bass'

claims.claim: smallmouth in the same lake used water about three times deeper than pickerel
claims.quote: smallmouth bass were predicted to occupy depths that are on average ~ 3 times deeper
claims.conditions: a model prediction (GAM D1) 'while holding all other variables constant', over Sept 2018–July 2019; 12 bass tagged, 5 of them died after the winter
claims.note: a modelled ratio, not a ratio of observed depths

claims.claim: in Milipsigate every tagged bass wintered at one of four sites shallower than 8 m
claims.quote: overwintered in areas that were not distinctly deep, all being shallower than 8 m
claims.conditions: by December and January all bass were at distinct wintering sites; four sites, each with at least two fish, in the north, south, east and west of the lake

claims.claim: the wintering sites were used at 2–6 m
claims.quote: winter dormant period from December to March, ranging from 2 to 6 m
claims.note: the same paragraph's model prediction reaches ~10 m in January, which does not sit well with sites all shallower than 8 m; the measured 2–6 m is the safer figure

claims.claim: the bass stayed "stationary throughout the winter until late March"
claims.quote: remaining stationary throughout the winter until late March
claims.conditions: horizontal positions at the four wintering sites; the analysis treats December–March as the bass's dormancy period

claims.claim: chain pickerel stay active near shore: 80 % of December positions were within 30 m of shore over rocky shallows
claims.quote: 80% of all positions for that month occurred within 30 m from the shore
claims.conditions: December 2018, all positions in the western part of the lake (bottom ≤ 4 m, p. 50); 'rocky' is the author's inference from bathymetry and personal observation ("appear to be selecting for coarse rocky nearshore habitat in December"), not from habitat data in the models; few fish (winter months averaged 94 pickerel positions)
claims.note: in January the pickerel moved over deeper water with bedrock (the south end has pockets of ~10–13 m), so 'near shore' holds for December more than for the whole winter

claims.claim: January and February pickerel positions clustered around islands
claims.conditions: January: 91 % of positions in the south-west of the array, around Hines Island; February: 97 % in the south-east, around Bird Island

claims.claim: tagged pickerel kept moving at a low level all winter, while the lake's smallmouth sat nearly still at four wintering sites
claims.quote: chain pickerel maintain low-level movement during the winter
claims.conditions: inferred from month-to-month shifts in where the clustered positions lay, not from measured swimming activity; the bass 'nearly sessile' at four sites

claims.claim: 79 % of June smallmouth positions lay within 50 m of shore
claims.quote: 79% of all positions in June were within 50 m
claims.conditions: within 50 m of the eastern or western shore; a share of positions (thinned to one per fish per hour), not of fish; at most 7 bass alive in June 2019 (5 of 12 died after the winter)

claims.claim: a share inflated by nesting males
claims.source_value: the thesis puts summer nearshore use down, tentatively, to choice of spawning habitat; it has no data by sex or on nests and does not say the 79 % is inflated
claims.location: p. 52 (PDF p. 64), §3.5; male guarding from late May to early July on p. 51 (PDF p. 63), citing Bain 1993 and DFO 1994
claims.quote: specific habitat use during the summer is likely driven by the selection of spawning habitat
claims.note: say 'which the author attributes to spawning' rather than 'inflated by nesting males'

claims.claim: smallmouth bass: within ~50 m of shore; a few deep wintering sites, nearly still Dec–Mar (Sergio 2026; Suski & Ridgway 2009)
claims.source_value: Milipsigate's four wintering sites were 'not distinctly deep', all shallower than 8 m and used at 2–6 m; 'nearly still Dec–Mar' and summer use within 50 m of shore are right
claims.quote: smallmouth bass were nearly sessile and occupied four distinct overwintering sites within the lake
claims.conditions: 'deep' wintering holds for Suski & Ridgway's Lake Opeongo, not for Sergio's lake (the thesis makes this same contrast)
claims.note: the comment should credit 'deep' to Suski & Ridgway only. Its 'rock, drop-offs and wood' and 'shallower at night' are not from Sergio

notes: Small samples: 18 pickerel tagged, but 3 were never detected, 1 died and 6 left within two weeks, leaving 3,584 filtered positions; 12 bass tagged, 5 died after the winter. Tagging was by angling from 1 September to 19 October 2018, which the author says inflated the autumn positions. Milipsigate is deeper (17 m), cooler and stratified, so its depth figures carry over to 4–5.5-m polymictic Hot Brook only in the relative sense the paper uses. The GAM terms (Table 2, p. 40) include bathymetry, which explains much of the depth use (bass F = 447, pickerel F = 44.6). Other values the rewrite could use: pickerel predicted at 0–2.5 m from October to April, ~8 m by August; bass at 0–15 m from spring to autumn; pickerel spawning thought to be ~2 weeks after ice-out at ~8–11 °C (p. 51, citing others).
